rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Determinants have anatomy. The **minor** Mᵢⱼ deletes row i and column j; the **cofactor** Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j)Mᵢⱼ stamps the checkerboard sign (+−+/−+−/++- pattern starting + at (1,1)); and the **Laplace expansion** |A| = Σ aᵢⱼCᵢⱼ works along any row or column — all choices agree (the 3×3 with cofactors 2, 2, −3, … expands to −3 along row 1 and column 1 alike).…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The zero-rich row*** - create zeros with row additions (which leave |A| unchanged), then expand along that row: the 3x3 slog collapses to one 2x2 determinant.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Determinant's Inner Machinery **Minors, cofactors and the adjoint** are the moving parts inside every determinant: the expansion theorem, the product rule |AB| = |A||B|, and the inverse formula A⁻¹ = adj A/|A|. This topic builds them carefully for 3×3 and beyond.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Minors and cofactors - **Minor Mᵢⱼ:** the determinant of the submatrix left after deleting row i and column j. - **Cofactor:** **Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j) Mᵢⱼ** — the checkerboard sign pattern (+ − + / − + − / + − +). - **Theorem (Laplace expansion):** |A| = Σⱼ aᵢⱼCᵢⱼ along **any** row or column — all choices give the same value; pick the row with the most zeros.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Sign checkerboard from + at (1,1). Expand along zeros. adj = transpose of cofactors. |kA| = k^n |A|. Cramer: replace one column at a time.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Find all cofactors of A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 10]] and evaluate |A| by expansion.** — **Cofactors (sign × minor):** C₁₁ = +(5·10 − 6·8) = +2; C₁₂ = −(4·10 − 6·7) = −(−2) = +2; C₁₃ = +(4·8 − 5·7) = −3; C₂₁ = −(2·10 − 3·8) = +4; C₂₂ = +(1·10 − 3·7) = −11; C₂₃ = −(1·8 − 2·7) = +6; C₃₁ = +(2·6 − 3·5) = −3; C₃₂ =…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Verify the adjoint identity A·adj A = |A|·I for A = [[2, 1], [3, 4]].** — **Cofactors:** C₁₁ = +4, C₁₂ = −3, C₂₁ = −1, C₂₂ = +2 ⟹ cofactor matrix [[4, −3], [−1, 2]] ⟹ **adj A = transpose = [[4, −1], [−3, 2]]**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In cofactor questions, write the sign and the minor separately before multiplying - merging them is where sign errors breed.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The adjoint identity A adj A = |A| I is the keystone: it is the inverse formula, the singularity obstruction, and a free check on adj computations all at once.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Minor M_ij: determinant after deleting row i, column j. Cofactor C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij (checkerboard + - + / - + - / + - +). Laplace expansion: |A| = sum a_ij C_ij along any row or column - all agree; choose the zero-rich row. Adjoint: transpose of the cofactor matrix, (adj A)_ij = C_ji.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Cramer's rule is why determinants predate matrices historically: each unknown is a ratio of two volumes.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Solve the system 2x + 3y = 8, x − y = −1 using Cramer's rule.** — **Coefficient determinant:** |A| = |2 3; 1 −1| = (2)(−1) − (3)(1) = −5 ≠ 0 ⟹ Cramer applies.…

rows.text: **adj A transposes the cofactor matrix:** using cofactors untransposed poisons every inverse computation.  ·  **|kA| = kⁿ|A|:** the scalar crosses each of n rows — for 3×3, |2A| = 8|A|, not 2|A|.  ·  ## 7.
